title: Message in the Static

beats.narrativeText: Atlas restores part of the outpost's communications array — and for the first time, there's more than text in the archive. There are voices.
One of the recovered audio files is a transmission from Dr. Elara Quinn — a name from the logs, now an actual voice, buried in static with whole sections missing.
The learner listens closely for repeated patterns, missing words and whatever context clues survive in the damaged message.
Piecing the surviving fragments together, the learner begins to make out what Dr. Quinn was actually trying to say.
The learner must fill in the missing sections and weigh up more than one possible interpretation of what the message means.
Out of everything reconstructed, the learner identifies exactly which facts the message actually confirms.
The learner reflects on what this first real message from Dr. Quinn reveals about the expedition's actions — and how different it feels to hear her, rather than just read about her.
One thing is now certain: the expedition deliberately shut down parts of the station. What's still missing is why — and Dr. Quinn's own recorded voice hasn't given that away yet.

activities.title: Decode Damaged Messages
activities.storyContext: A heavily corrupted transmission from Dr. Elara Quinn has been recovered from the restored communications array — the first time her own words, not just her name, have surfaced.
activities.instructions: Read through the damaged transmission carefully and note any words or phrases you can make out, even ones that seem like fragments on their own.
activities.output: Notes on what can be understood from the damaged transmission.

activities.title: Complete Missing Sections
activities.storyContext: Large portions of the message are missing entirely — reconstructing them means working from context, not guesswork.
activities.instructions: Use repeated patterns and context clues from the parts you can read to suggest what the missing sections might say.
activities.output: A reconstructed version of the message.

activities.title: Compare Possible Interpretations
activities.storyContext: More than one interpretation of the reconstructed message can sound plausible — that's exactly why it's worth comparing them properly rather than settling on the first one.
activities.instructions: Compare a few possible interpretations of the message and decide which is best supported by the evidence, not just which one sounds most dramatic.
activities.output: Notes comparing possible interpretations of the message.

activities.title: Identify Confirmed Facts
activities.storyContext: Not everything in the reconstructed message can be fully trusted — some of it is Dr. Quinn's own words, and some of it is the learner's best reconstruction.
activities.instructions: List only the facts from the message that are confirmed by clear evidence, leaving out anything you're still just reconstructing.
activities.output: A list of confirmed facts from the message.

activities.title: Create a Coded Message
activities.storyContext: Now that the learner understands how coded messages work, they can create one of their own.
activities.instructions: Create a coded message of your own for another Explorer to solve.

activities.title: Recovering Damaged Historical Records
activities.storyContext: Recovering this message is similar to real scientific and historical work.
activities.instructions: Find out how scientists recover damaged historical documents or radio transmissions.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What do you think the expedition was hiding when they deliberately shut down parts of the station — and what makes you think that?

discussionPoints: What clues helped you fill in the missing parts of the message?
Why might the expedition have deliberately gone quiet?
parentGuide.assessment: Look for reasonable, evidence-based guesses for the missing sections, and a clear list of confirmed facts.

completionCriteria: Damaged message decoded, missing sections completed, and confirmed facts identified.
